items.stem: A teammate is assigned "Do the research" with no other detail. After a week she says she is not sure what is left. What would have helped most?

options.text: Giving her one more week to finish all the research.
options.feedback: More time does not tell her what finished means. She would still be unsure after another week.

options.text: Splitting it into pieces, each with a clear end point.
options.feedback: Small pieces with clear ends let her say what is done and what is left.

options.text: Asking two more people to also do the same research.
options.feedback: Two more people on an unclear job make it more confusing. Each of them would pick a different meaning of finished.

items.stem: In the booth plan, Buy materials needs the layout first. The layout is finished two days late. Which jobs slip?

options.text: Only Buy materials, because it is the only job that names the layout.
options.feedback: Run the morning shift needs the materials, and Record sign-ups needs the shift. Both move too.

options.text: Every job, including the shift schedule and the sign-up sheet.
options.feedback: The schedule and the sign-up sheet need no layout, so they keep their dates.

options.text: Buy materials, Run the morning shift and Record sign-ups.
options.feedback: Each of these waits for the layout, directly or through another job. Delays travel along the chain of dependencies.

items.stem: The booth plan needs 5 days with 3 people. A fourth person joins. How many days does the plan need now?

options.text: Still 5 days, since the longest chain stays the same.
options.feedback: Design layout, Buy materials, Run the morning shift and Record sign-ups take 5 days one after another, however many people help.

options.text: 4 days, since a fourth person finishes more of the work.
options.feedback: An extra person helps only with jobs that can run at the same time. The jobs in the chain run one after another.

options.text: 3 days, since the work is shared among four people.
options.feedback: A job cannot start before the jobs it needs are done, so the plan cannot shrink below its longest chain.

items.stem: A one-day delay hits one job. Which delay makes the whole project finish a day late?

options.text: Make signs, because it takes two days like Buy materials.
options.feedback: Make signs has a day to spare. It can run a day late and still be done before the morning shift starts.

options.text: Brief volunteers, because the morning shift cannot start without it.
options.feedback: The briefing ends on day 2 and the morning shift starts on day 4, so one more day still fits.

options.text: Design sign-up sheet, because it is the smallest job.
options.feedback: The sheet is needed only for the last job, so it has days to spare.

options.text: Buy materials, because it sits on the longest chain.
options.feedback: Every job after it waits, and no other job can cover the gap.
